rubric_notes: Correct hierarchy and all four curated families plus a.22.1.0 with sunids, matching bundle. Family vs superfamily distinction handled correctly; states fold alone would not imply homology and that a.22 has no second superfamily. Explicit limit that superfamily membership does not license function transfer (TAF/NC2/NF-Y/CHRAC/SOS not nucleosomal). Correctly separates H1/H5 (a.4.5.13), H-NS (a.155.1), modifying enzymes. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families with sunids, superfamily a.204.1 as lowest shared node, boundaries and annotation caveats match the bundle. Explains that the superfamily, not the fold, encodes the homology hypothesis; rejects PR-ATP substrate and histidine-pathway transfer, assumption that SSo12199 is active, kinetic/regulatory transfer, template use and domain-boundary equivalence. Lists external evidence needed. Complete.

Correct families, superfamily, fold, class and sunids supported by bundle; correctly notes two c.55.1 domains per chain. Infers remote homology with conserved two-lobe architecture and ASKHA phosphate/adenosine motifs, cautiously transfers only general nucleotide-binding and hinge features, and rejects transfer of substrate, regulatory sites, oligomeric state, and catalytic residues without validated alignment; template limits and fold-level non-homology stated; automated-match caveat included. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Biological interpretation complete: divergent evolution from a common ancestor with functional divergence, superfamily comment used as the homology rationale, fold-only siblings not read as homologous, explicit refusal of function transfer and list of family-level evidence needed. Factual: claims pairwise comparison of d1fhaa_/d1riba_/d1jkua_ returned 'same_superfamily, no caveats', but no compare endpoint output is in the bundle (only sids/parents/annotations/homology); lowest shared node is derivable but the cited comparison result is unsupported. Omits AMB4284-like from family list (minor). Other identifiers supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families and superfamily; example domains d1ag6a_, d1shxa_, d5n0ya1 and their annotations (cu complex, automated matches) match bundle; pairwise lowest-shared-node claim is consistent with retrieved parents. Superfamily homology correctly contrasted with b.6.2 fold-only; copper/ET refused with required evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families, sunids, superfamily/fold placement and sibling families, all supported by bundle; homology record (sf, true) cited correctly. Clear evolutionary interpretation (scaffold repurposed as interaction module, homology not sequence similarity). Names every unsafe transfer: conjugation to UBX/RBD, Ras binding, p97 binding, binding-site residues, within-family differences, fold-level non-inference including MoaD/ThiS trap. States need for external sequence/experimental evidence. No material errors.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families c.23.1.1/c.23.1.4/c.23.1.5 under c.23.1 with sunids and Pfam PF03709 matching the bundle; superfamily-level remote homology stated with fold-level caveat; KaiA 'lacks canonical receiver' annotation used; explicitly rejects transfer of phosphorylation/kinase signaling, Mg2+ binding, and decarboxylase activity; wing identified as non-catalytic accessory domain (recruitment). Minor: describes ODC catalytic domains in eukaryotic terms (alanine racemase-like barrel) although the classified c.23.1.4 entry is Lactobacillus ODC; not a SCOPe classification claim, so not penalized.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Verified lineage and sunids, five superfamilies with comments, b.84.1.1 biotinyl/lipoyl family, two protein entries with correct domains and boundaries, PubMed xref, homology-endpoint contrast between fold (not implied) and b.84.5 (implied, scope sf). Correctly describes the bulge as an insertion inside the discontinuous P-loop domain. Evolutionary claim stated at correct strength: positive homology within b.84.5.1 (V1/A1 naming not an evolutionary split), deliberately no claim toward b.84.1-b.84.4, with divergence vs convergence left unadjudicated. Rejects cross-superfamily function/template transfer. 3a5c chain-A domain layout is not in the bundle but matches the bundled 3gqb pattern.

Correct three superfamilies with sunids; correct fold-vs-superfamily inference, 'possible link' cited as not a merge, convergence stated only as possibility, external evidence named. Noncentral family-level imprecision: describes f.21.2 as 'FrdC/FrdD two-chain and single-chain SdhC-type' families, reversing single-chain (FrdC, f.21.2.1) vs two-chain (SdhC/SdhD, f.21.2.2).

Family sunids, superfamily/fold/class lineage, fold comment, family comments and PF02254 match the bundle. Gives the correct per-level reading, identifies the superfamily grouping as a remote but positive homology claim and the different-family placement as evidence against close relationship, and states that the shared scaffold predicts binding-site geometry but nothing reliable about ligand, catalysis, oligomeric state or role. Covers template limits, fragment nature of SCOPe domains, automated-match caveat and the external evidence needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct same-family placement (k.40.1.1, sunid 100905) and lineage, good discussion of class k and the mechanical homology flag, appropriate no-transfer limits. Does not mention the 'not a true family' curator comment (family annotations not retrieved); decisive annotation ignored, bio ceiling <=2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Must_include met: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 singleton fold verified vs 1f8y c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1 shared superfamily verified; frames the change as dissolution of a fold and re-parenting of a preserved family sunid, i.e. a new homology hypothesis, explicitly separating the tag-split boundary change. Evolutionary strength and function/template caveats are correct, and it notes shared fold alone would not imply homology. Factual imprecisions: states the move was made in the 'SCOP 1.73/1.75 timeframe' when it was already in 1.71 (not queried), and labels the 1.69 superfamily with its later name N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like. Noncentral, so factual 3.

All must_include met with supported lineage and sunids for d1a14h2 and d1a14h1; explicit rejection of tag similarity as homology, explanation of class-l level semantics, empty xrefs cited correctly, appropriate caveat that even V-set hits support ancestry not antigen specificity. No material errors.

Accurate 1.75 single whole-chain domain with full lineage and accurate 2.08 pair with correct sunids, sccs, and boundaries, including the class-level move of the N-terminal unit. Strong modularity inference supported by the populated PA14-like superfamily and the single-family C-terminal superfamily, with explicit level calibration, refusal of function transfer, warning against class-level prefiltering, and conservative reading of absence. Does not identify 2.04 as the release where the split entered, the one missing noncentral release detail.

All five domains with correct SIDs, boundaries, sccs and sibling families; new fold d.394 singleton verified; c.55.3.14 pre-existence shown via species nodes. Mosaic interpretation with group II intron hypothesis attributed to literature, superfamily vs family distinction, and explicit rejection of catalytic and acetyl-lysine function transfer; Jab1/MPN omission and cryo-EM limits noted. No material errors.

Covers all three required elements: common family a.298.1.1 with correct lineage, length differences as integer multiples of the repeat, and both the quoted 're' inconsistency definition and the canonical repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 with d4cj9a_ as representative. Explains why a single 34-residue hairpin is not treated as an independent domain, ranks homology strength correctly across family, superfamily and fold, uses approximate rather than fixed repeat counts, and warns that coverage statistics between these domains mislead. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Endpoint metadata correct and evidence-backed. Cites frozen 2.08-stable pinned to release=2.08; preserves exact dated periodic label when results depend on newly added entries. Periodic semantics correct: automated additions to existing nodes without re-curating or adding new folds/superfamilies, moving target with date as version. Appropriate caveat that automated assignments are not curator-verified.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Concise and correct: same family a.47.2.1, ms flag and spectrin comment, 1dn1 obsolete/automated match with d3c98b_ as curated full domain, a.47 defined by four helices so the fragments' fold is a consequence of homology to the complete domain; ms flag as a warning against structural transfer; fold similarity across a.47 superfamilies and to a.7 is not homology; function (Munc18 binding, closed state) not inferable from fragments; states that a new three-helix fragment needs sequence homology or a complete-domain structure. All identifiers match bundle.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Central conclusion and level semantics correct; gives alternative (ancient divergence vs independent recruitment) for c.2/c.3/c.4 and a good evidence-integration list. However it states flatly that c.2.1 vs c.1.7 vs c.82.1 vs c.71.1 'represent independent inventions' and that NAD(P) oxidoreductases are polyphyletic, without the caveat that separate SCOPe placement is absence of a homology assertion rather than proof of convergence. Identifiers (c.1.7 51430, c.71 53596, c.82 53719, c.23.5 52218, d.81 55346, c.2.1/c.4.1 family lists) match the bundle; correctly notes c.2.1/c.3.1 superfamily nodes carry no comments in 2.08.

Gets the relationship change right: different folds and superfamilies in 2.04, shared superfamily b.18.1 with different families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 now, framed as probable rather than proven common ancestry. Cites the curated PubMed 17977833 comment, the jelly-roll sandwich architecture, and the shared non-catalytic C-terminal targeting role, and is explicit that fold alone would not justify homology and that collagen binding, calcium and insecticidal activity must not transfer. Deduction for asserting a deterministic lineage-comparison result of same_superfamily with caveats_present false, which no retrieved response in its bundle provides, and for presenting superposition and strand-order specifics as the curatorial basis without retrieved support.

Homology, hf semantics, template and training limits, quality comparison and wild-type alternatives are all handled well. However it misreads the 'complexed with nhe' comment as a DNA complex and builds on it, calling 1p7j DNA-bound and a suitable reference for DNA-recognition geometry; 1p7j contains no DNA (NHE is a buffer heterogen). This unsupported functional-context inference costs one point on each subscore. Stratification is implied (exclude as a.4 positive) rather than stated as retaining the label.

Lineage, fr flag, comment, 50-residue ATOM sequence, complete siblings (d2hfta2, d1boya2, d6r2wt2, d1jpst2, etc.) match bundle; quality values correct. Reasoning complete: homology unaffected, asymmetric alignment with coverage relative to observed length, fragment excluded/down-weighted in profiles, boundaries not biological, complete sibling chosen by AEROSPACI as representative, d1uc6a1 usable complete-domain representative, fragment only for local analyses, diversity artefacts, protein-level redundancy, no function transfer, external evidence named. Noncentral factual error: calls 1o5d a uPA/tissue-factor complex (partner domains indicate factor VIIa). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Recommends new superfamily in existing fold; family = close common ancestor claim, superfamily = probable ancestry, fold = topology only with no homology implied; new fold only if core arrangement/connectivity genuinely differs. Classification framed as revisable hypothesis requiring integrated structural, functional and profile evidence; single alignment score insufficient; rejects function/active-site transfer from fold-mates; notes manual curation. c.1 sunid 51350 and superfamily listing supported by bundle (34 superfamilies consistent with has_more=false listing through c.1.33 plus truncation). No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct fold/superfamily/families with supported sunids and representatives (d1atpe_, d1j7la_, d1e8xa4 boundaries) and PI3K accessory domains (a.118.1.6, b.7.1.1, d.15.1.5). Clear hierarchy of inference strength (fold < superfamily < family), conserved Mg-ATP catalytic chemistry, ATP-grasp/PIPK comment handled as remark. Explicitly refuses substrate transfer (noting mTOR within d.144.1.4) and regulation transfer, warns against cross-family templates and automated matches. Evidence requirements complete. No material errors.
